HAS PrepperDisk topluluğun emeğiyle büyüyor. Her katkı gerçek bir Raspberry Pi 5 üzerinde denendi ve sonra eklendi. Emeği geçen herkese teşekkürler.

HAS PrepperDisk grows with the community's work. Every contribution below was tested on a real Raspberry Pi 5 before it was merged. Thank you to everyone who helped.

 PR Katkıda bulunan / Contributor Ne getirdi What it added 
 --- --- --- --- 
 3 @turer73, doğrulama / verified by @volthdl Kaldırılmış ZIM adlarını düzeltti, Türkçe içerikleri (Vikikitap, Vikisöz, Vikikaynak, Vikisözlük, PhET, iFixit) ekledi, sürümleri Kiwix kataloğundan bulup her indirmeyi SHA-256 ile doğrulayan indirme betiği Fixed retired ZIM names, added Turkish content (Wikibooks, Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wiktionary, PhET, iFixit), catalog-based versions and SHA-256 verification for every download 
 10 @Proxy34 Ana sayfada telefonun değil kutunun saati, ZIM dosyalarının doğru eşleşmesi ve README düzeltmeleri Homepage shows the box's clock instead of the phone's, correct ZIM matching and README fixes 
 11 @Proxy34 AFAD, CDC ve EPA kaynaklı, internetsiz açılan Türkçe acil durum sayfası Turkish emergency page sourced from AFAD, CDC and EPA, works offline 
 12 @efeesrefinal Kutunun durumunu tek komutla gösteren salt okunur sağlık kontrolü ( status.sh ) Read-only health check that shows the box's state in one command ( status.sh ) 
 13 @efeesrefinal Her PR'da kabuk betiklerini otomatik denetleyen ShellCheck CI ShellCheck CI that checks the shell scripts on every PR 
 16 @Proxy34 Telefonda rahat okunan ve parmakla kolay basılan ana sayfa Homepage that is easy to read and tap on phones 
 17 @Proxy34 Disk dolarken, SSD yıpranırken ya da güç yetersizken ana sayfada uyarı Homepage warnings when the disk is filling up, the SSD is wearing out or power is insufficient 
 28 @isihussain İnternetsiz ortamda saati korumak için RTC pili notu RTC battery note for keeping the time without internet 
 29 @isihussain Windows'ta klonlanan betiklerin Pi'de bozulmaması için satır sonu ayarı ( .gitattributes ) Line-ending rules ( .gitattributes ) so scripts cloned on Windows still run on the Pi 

İnceleme ve testleriyle açık PR'lara destek olan @volthdl, @FurkanKY, @Proxy34 ve @ramazansancar'a da ayrıca teşekkürler.

Special thanks also to @volthdl, @FurkanKY, @Proxy34 and @ramazansancar for reviewing and testing open PRs.

 English

An offline knowledge archive on a Raspberry Pi 5. Wikipedia, maps, medical references and repair guides, served over the Pi's own Wi-Fi hotspot. Any phone or laptop that joins the network can open them in a browser. No internet needed.

Built on Internet-in-a-Box and Kiwix. This repo adds a ready-made configuration, helper scripts and a custom homepage.

 Hardware

 Part Notes 
 --- --- 
 Raspberry Pi 5 (4 GB or 8 GB) 
 M.2 NVMe HAT + NVMe SSD (256 GB+) Content lives here 
 microSD card (32 GB+) Operating system 
 5V/5A USB-C power supply The official one is recommended 
 Active cooler The Pi 5 and SSD get warm 
 Ethernet cable Recommended during install 
 RTC battery (optional) Keeps system time offline (e.g. official SC1163) 

 RTC battery note: Without internet access, the Pi 5 cannot sync time via NTP. When power is lost, the internal RTC clock resets unless a backup battery is connected to the J5 (BAT) connector. If you use the official rechargeable Panasonic ML-2020 battery (SC1163), enable trickle-charging by adding dtparam=rtc bbat vchg=3000000 to /boot/firmware/config.txt . (Do not enable charging if using standard non-rechargeable CR2032 cells). 

 

 Installation

 1. Operating system. Use Raspberry Pi Imager to flash Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit) to the SD card. In Imager's settings, enable SSH and set a username and password. Boot the Pi with the SSD attached and connect it to your router with Ethernet.

 2. Update and get this repo. 
 

 3. Mount the SSD at /library . Find the disk name with lsblk ; it is usually nvme0n1 . If the disk is not ext4 it will be formatted, and the script asks before doing so.
 

 4. Install. The script asks for the Wi-Fi name and password, then installs Internet-in-a-Box (30–60 min). If the Pi reboots or the install stops, run the same command again. It continues where it left off.
 
During the install Internet-in-a-Box asks three things of its own: a new password for the iiab-admin user (used for http:// /admin , write it down), a key press to confirm you will re-run the command if something goes wrong, and at the end Enter to reboot. After the reboot run sudo ./install.sh once more; it skips the finished part and installs the homepage.

 5. Download content. Edit config/content.conf to choose what to download, then run the script below. The defaults need about 160 GB, and downloads can take many hours. If a download is interrupted, re-run the script and it resumes. The script looks up the newest version of each ZIM in the Kiwix catalog, checks free disk space before each download and verifies every file against its SHA-256 checksum.
 

 6. Maps. Open http:// /admin (user iiab-admin ), go to the maps section of the Install Content menu and choose the regions you want.

 7. Use it. Join the Wi-Fi network you created and open 

 Optional: internet over a USB Wi-Fi adapter

The Pi's built-in Wi-Fi is dedicated to the hotspot. If the Pi needs internet temporarily (updates, new content) and there is no Ethernet cable, add a cheap USB Wi-Fi adapter as a second card. Adapters with the MediaTek MT7601U chip work out of the box.

1. Plug the adapter in, preferably into a black USB 2.0 port. The blue USB 3.0 ports can interfere with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.
2. Join the Pi's hotspot from your laptop and connect: ssh user@10.10.10.10 
3. Connect the adapter (usually wlan1 ) to a Wi-Fi network:
 
4. When you are done, remove the connection: sudo nmcli connection delete temp-wifi 

 Never run sudo iiab-network while a USB Wi-Fi adapter is plugged in. It may move the hotspot onto the adapter.

install.title: Installation
install.html:
1. Operating system. Use Raspberry Pi Imager to flash Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit) to the SD card. In Imager's settings, enable SSH and set a username and password. Boot the Pi with the SSD attached and connect it to your router with Ethernet.

2. Update and get this repo.

sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y git
git clone https://github.com/schematrix/HAS_Prepper_Disk.git
cd HAS_Prepper_Disk
chmod +x install.sh scripts/*.sh

3. Mount the SSD at /library. Find the disk name with lsblk; it is usually nvme0n1. If the disk is not ext4 it will be formatted, and the script asks before doing so.

sudo ./scripts/setup-ssd.sh /dev/nvme0n1

4. Install. The script asks for the Wi-Fi name and password, then installs Internet-in-a-Box (30–60 min). If the Pi reboots or the install stops, run the same command again. It continues where it left off.

sudo ./install.sh

During the install Internet-in-a-Box asks three things of its own: a new password for the iiab-admin user (used for http://<pi-ip>/admin, write it down), a key press to confirm you will re-run the command if something goes wrong, and at the end Enter to reboot. After the reboot run sudo ./install.sh once more; it skips the finished part and installs the homepage.

5. Download content. Edit config/content.conf to choose what to download, then run the script below. The defaults need about 160 GB, and downloads can take many hours. If a download is interrupted, re-run the script and it resumes. The script looks up the newest version of each ZIM in the Kiwix catalog, checks free disk space before each download and verifies every file against its SHA-256 checksum.

sudo ./scripts/download-content.sh

6. Maps. Open http://<pi-ip>/admin (user iiab-admin), go to the maps section of the Install Content menu and choose the regions you want.

7. Use it. Join the Wi-Fi network you created and open http://box.lan/home.
